key_insight: Collaborative Theory of Mind (CToM) improves multi-turn LLM collaboration by predicting user replies and using those predictions to self-revise before responding.
engineering_relevance: The approach can make assistant systems more accurate and interaction-efficient in real workflows that require iterative feedback, such as math solving, coding, and drafting.
method: Draft an answer, then predict how the user is likely to respond.
Use the predicted reply to revise the draft internally before finalizing the response.
Train with a user-reply prediction loss plus GRPO to optimize both task quality and interaction efficiency.
evidence_signal: Across mathematical reasoning, coding, and writing tasks, CToM outperformed baselines, including improving collaborative math accuracy from 74.1% to 79.6% over naive GRPO.
watch_item: The method adds an extra prediction module and training objective, so its gains may depend on reliable user-response modeling and may be less robust when user feedback is noisy or out-of-distribution.
paper_title: Collaborative Theory of Mind: Learning to Self-Revise by Anticipating User Responses
